tool.name: BLAST Search
tool.description: run local blastn or blastp against a FASTA subject file
tool.command: #set $blast_task_arg = "" #if $program.program_id == "blastn" and str($program.blast_task) not in ["", "None"]: #set $blast_task_arg = "--blast-task '%s'" % $program.blast_task #end if #set $blast_binary_arg = "" #if str($blast_binary) not in ["", "None"]: #set $blast_binary_arg = "--blast-binary '%s'" % $blast_binary #end if #set $makeblastdb_binary_arg = "" #if str($makeblastdb_binary) not in ["", "None"]: #set $makeblastdb_binary_arg = "--makeblastdb-binary '%s'" % $makeblastdb_binary #end if python '$__tool_directory__/blast_search.py' --program '$program.program_id' --query '$query' --subject '$subject' --output '$report' --output-format '$output_format' --evalue '$evalue' --max-target-seqs '$max_target_seqs' --num-threads '$num_threads' $blast_task_arg $blast_binary_arg $makeblastdb_binary_arg
tool.help:
This first BLAST integration runs local BLAST+ searches inside Galaxy.
Included programs =================
- ``blastn`` for nucleotide queries against nucleotide subjects - ``blastp`` for protein queries against protein subjects
How this wrapper works ======================
Instead of requiring a pre-built BLAST database datatype, this tool accepts a subject FASTA file from Galaxy history, builds a temporary local database with ``makeblastdb``, and then runs the selected BLAST program.
Outputs =======
- ``Tabular``: BLAST outfmt 6 with standard alignment columns - ``Pairwise``: the classic text report
Admin notes ===========
This wrapper expects NCBI BLAST+ executables to be available in the job environment. In this repository the recommended deployment is a dedicated Conda environment, wired through ``config/job_conf.yml``.
